newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM says government safe despite problems.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM says government safe despite problems.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday that his centre-left government is safe despite a regional party saying it plans to quit the United Front coalition.
"I do not see any possibility or any probability or any chance of a strain on the government," he told Asian News International in a videotaped television interview.
He said he had spoken to leaders of the Tamil Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party since it said on Monday that it planned to quit the government.
"I would like to assure the nation that things are going smoothly," he said in reaction to the party's decision.

"I am sure we would be able to sort it out in the next meeting of the steering committee (of the United Front)," Gujral said. "I am absolutely certain we will be able to bridge the difficulties." He did not say when the meeting would be held.
The DMK said the coalition had compromised its dignity by allowing some partners to force their own agenda in the alliance. But it said it would continue to support the government.

It did not offer further explanation but the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), an influential alliance partner, insists that a breakaway group of Gujral's Janata Dal party should be removed from the coalition.
Industry Minister Murasoli Maran, one of four DMK ministers, told reporters after meeting the prime minister the issue would be resolved.
"We will meet at the steering committee meeting and we will thrash it out," Maran told reporters. "I think you jumped to a conclusion -- we said we were contemplating (pulling out)."
The DMK accounts for less than 20 of the United Front's 178 lawmakers in India's 545-seat lower house of federal parliament. The coalition's survival depends on the Congress party's 140 members.
There was a split on July 5 in the Janata Dal, whose leader Laloo Prasad Yadav formed a breakaway Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) but stayed on in the 15-party alliance.

Yadav broke away alleging malpractice in internal party elections held on July 3, but said he had nothing against Gujral, whose government his group continues to support. Three of his loyalists are in the Gujral government.

But the CPI-M targeted Yadav, who has been indicted by federal police in a $280 million corruption scandal. It said Yadav should resign as the chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, or his group should be expelled from the coalition.
Yadav says he is innocent and has refused to resign. On Tuesday, his state government group won a vote of confidence in the Bihar state assembly.
"We will persuade and even pressurise the prime minister to keep the RJD away from the United Front," the Press Trust of India quoted CPI-M general secretary Harkishen Singh Surjeet as saying.
Gujral has so far stonewalled communist attempts to force Yadav's group out of the coalition.
The United Front was formed last year with the support of the Congress party to keep the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which controls 193 votes in parliament, out of power.
